metadata.case_name: CHUNG SUNG YONG v. AU SZE HUNG, CHRISTOPHER AND ANOTHER

plaintiff.occupation_before: owner of a family inn in Seoul

injuries.description: fractures to his left shoulder bones
source: The plaintiff sustained injuries to the tibia and fibula in his left leg and bones in his left shoulder.
injuries.icd_description: Multiple fractures of clavicle, scapula or humerus

injuries.description: fractures to the tibia and fibula in his left leg; imperfect union with angulation of 5° to 10° and shortness of the left leg by half an inch; muscle damage causing weakness in the left leg
source: The plaintiff sustained injuries to the tibia and fibula in his left leg and bones in his left shoulder.
Dr Li also took the view that the imperfect union of the bones in the left leg produced an angle (angulation) which had been reduced to 5° to 10°. 5° - 10° would not affect the ankle joint.
Dr Li further explained that given time the shortness of the left leg by half an inch would not cause any noticeable limbing in walking.
There was some muscle damage in the accident causing weakness in the left leg. That would be permanent to a degree.

manifestations.description: He was knocked unconscious for three days.
some muscle damage in the accident causing weakness in the left leg
stiffness of the left leg and the ankle joint
running and squatting would be hampered
shortness of the left leg by half an inch
He could not clean his left leg which was, as described by the plaintiff, decaying.

treatments_received: metal fixator applied to leg (external fixator with metal pins)
treatments_future: further physiotherapy (three months after bone graft)

losses.description: Dr Li's ultimate assessment was 3% for the left shoulder and 4% for the left leg and ankle giving a total of 7% permanent disability.
Dr Li's ultimate assessment was 3% for the left shoulder and 4% for the left leg and ankle giving a total of 7% permanent disability.

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: The plaintiff skied before the accident. That past-time is now beyond his reach.
running and squatting would be hampered; stiffness of the left leg and the ankle joint would improve gradually within the five years after the injury.

losses.category: Loss of ability to do domestic tasks
losses.description: He could not clean his left leg which was, as described by the plaintiff, decaying.
I accept his evidence that he is no longer in a position to carry on with his former calling as a result of his injuries.
